title: Cyberpunk 2077 Life Paths Explained: Corpo, Nomad or Streetkid?
description: Cyberpunk 2077 life paths explained: what Corpo, Nomad and Streetkid change, what stays the same, and which origin makes the most sense for a first playthrough.
body:
Cyberpunk 2077 asks you to choose between Corpo, Nomad and Streetkid before you have seen much of Night City. The choice looks like a class system, but it is better understood as V’s background. Your life path changes the opening, adds recurring dialogue options and gives some scenes a different perspective, but it does not lock you into a combat build or a separate main campaign.

That means there is no mechanically mandatory “best” life path. Pick the version of V whose relationship with Night City sounds most interesting to you: an insider from the corporate world, an outsider arriving from beyond the city, or someone who already knows its streets.

If you are still learning Night City’s broader systems, start with our [Cyberpunk 2077 beginner’s guide](/stories/cyberpunk-2077-beginners-guide/). Once you are ready to shape V mechanically, our [attributes and perks beginner guide](/stories/cyberpunk-2077-best-attributes-perks-beginners/) explains the modern progression system.
author: Rouane Mounssif
imageAlt: Cyberpunk 2077 promotional artwork used as the feature image for Neural Critic’s guide to the Corpo, Nomad and Streetkid life paths.

contentBlocks.text:
Each life path gives V a different prologue before the main storyline converges. After that, the paths share the same central campaign, but background-specific dialogue choices continue to appear in conversations.

Those options can add context, let V recognize details that another background might miss, or change the tone of a response. They are best thought of as role-playing knowledge rather than a permanent gameplay bonus.

Your life path does not decide whether V becomes a hacker, a close-range fighter, a stealth-focused character or something else. The attribute and perk systems remain separate from the origin you choose.
contentBlocks.heading: What Does a Life Path Actually Change?

contentBlocks.text:
Nomad begins outside Night City, making it the easiest background to recommend to players who want V’s knowledge to grow alongside their own. The opening frames the city as somewhere you are entering rather than somewhere your character already understands.

That makes unfamiliar districts, factions and customs feel natural from a role-playing perspective. Nomad-specific dialogue tends to reflect experience with life beyond the city and with the communities that exist outside its corporate center.

Choose Nomad if you like the idea of arriving with fewer assumptions and discovering Night City as an outsider.
contentBlocks.heading: Nomad — The Outsider’s View of Night City

contentBlocks.text:
Streetkid starts from the opposite position. This V has a personal relationship with Night City and speaks like someone who understands its neighborhoods, reputations and informal rules.

The background fits players who want their protagonist to feel immediately embedded in the setting. Streetkid dialogue can make V sound more familiar with local people and situations without changing the fundamental shape of the campaign.

Choose it if you want Night City to feel like V’s home rather than a new environment.
contentBlocks.heading: Streetkid — V Already Knows the City

contentBlocks.text:
Corpo begins inside the powerful corporate structure that shapes much of Cyberpunk 2077’s world. This version of V understands the language, pressure and internal politics of that environment from personal experience.

Corpo-specific dialogue can therefore give conversations a sharper insider perspective when corporations, contracts or professional power games are involved.

It is a strong choice if you want the story to carry an additional contrast between where V starts and the much less controlled life that follows.
contentBlocks.heading: Corpo — The Corporate Insider

contentBlocks.text:
No. Your life path and your character build are separate decisions. Corpo does not force an Intelligence-focused character, Nomad does not force a physical build, and Streetkid does not commit you to stealth or any particular combat style.

Cyberpunk 2077’s modern progression system is built around five attributes and their perk trees, while cyberware has become another major part of build identity since Update 2.0. You can develop any of those systems regardless of your origin.

This is the main reason beginners should not choose a life path based on a build guide.
contentBlocks.heading: Does Life Path Change Your Build?

contentBlocks.text:
They create different beginnings and recurring moments of flavor rather than three separate campaigns. Once the prologue has done its job, the major story structure comes together.

That does not make the choice meaningless. Background dialogue can change how V reads a situation and can make the same scene feel different across playthroughs. But you should not expect three entirely different questlines from choosing three origins.

Think of life path as the lens through which V enters the same larger story.
contentBlocks.heading: Do Life Paths Create Different Main Stories?

contentBlocks.text:
Nomad has a small role-playing advantage for newcomers because both player and character are approaching Night City from the outside. Streetkid is best if you want V to feel at home in the city immediately, while Corpo is the strongest contrast if you are interested in the setting’s corporate power structures.

None is objectively stronger in the progression system. The best first choice is simply the one whose starting identity makes you most curious about the character you are going to play.

If you return for another run, changing life path is a useful way to give familiar conversations a slightly different perspective without rebuilding the entire game.
contentBlocks.heading: Which Life Path Is Best for a First Playthrough?

conclusion:
Choose Nomad, Streetkid or Corpo for the version of V you want to inhabit, not for a hidden statistical advantage. Life paths shape the opening and add background-specific dialogue, but the modern Cyberpunk 2077 build system remains open regardless of origin.

For a newcomer, Nomad offers the most natural discovery arc, Streetkid provides immediate familiarity with Night City, and Corpo gives you an insider’s view of its corporate machinery. All three lead into the same larger campaign, so there is no wrong first choice.
